issues.legal_issue: A civil suit challenging the fact or validity of a widow’s adoption is not barred merely because the adoption has been confirmed by the government.
material_facts: The estate holder died without a male issue by birth or adoption.
A widow claimed to have adopted a son, and the adoption was confirmed by the government.
A claimant brought a civil suit seeking a declaration that the adoption had not occurred or was invalid, rather than seeking confirmation of the adoption.
issues.conclusion: The suit challenging the fact or validity of the adoption was within the jurisdiction of the civil court and was not barred by the Regulation.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 23 and 119 of the Ajmer Land and Revenue Regulation, 1877, confirmation is a statutory condition for treating a widow’s adoption as valid for succession to the estate, but it does not make an adoption valid if it is otherwise invalid under general law. Section 119 protects the confirmation itself from impeachment; it does not make the underlying facts and acts preceding confirmation conclusive or bar a civil court from examining the adoption’s validity. Section 119 also does not bar a suit that seeks a declaration about the adoption rather than an order the government is empowered to make. The court relied on the general principle that civil court jurisdiction is not excluded unless the law does so expressly or by clear implication. No earlier cases are cited as relied upon.

rule.if: civil_suit_concerning_adoption and widow_adoption_confirmed and suit_challenges_adoption_fact_or_validity and not suit_seeks_confirmation_order

predicates.civil_suit_concerning_adoption: A claimant brought a civil suit concerning whether an heir had been adopted.
predicates.widow_adoption_confirmed: The government confirmed an adoption claimed to have been made by a widow.
predicates.suit_challenges_adoption_fact_or_validit: The claimant asked the civil court to decide whether the adoption occurred or was legally valid.
predicates.suit_seeks_confirmation_order: The claimant asked the civil court to grant the confirmation of the adoption.

issues.definition: When a civil suit challenges the fact or validity of a confirmed widow’s adoption without seeking an order confirming it, the civil court may examine the adoption’s fact or validity.

issues.legal_issue: A civil claim to determine the right to succeed to an estate in a case not governed by the male-issue succession rule must follow the prescribed administrative process or obtain authorization for a civil suit.
material_facts: The estate holder was alleged to have died without a male issue by birth or adoption.
The claimant also sought a declaration that he was the nearest kin and heir entitled to succeed to the estate.
The court treated that succession claim, if it arose in a case not provided for by the male-issue rule, as falling within the separate succession procedure.
issues.conclusion: The succession claim prima facie attracted section 24 and had to comply with its conditions; the court expressed no opinion on the merits of that claim.
issues.legal_principle: Section 24 of the Ajmer Land and Revenue Regulation, 1877, provides that a succession question arising in a case not provided for by section 23 is to be decided by the government or an appointed officer. The government may instead issue a certificate that the matter is proper for determination by a civil court, in which case the certificate-holder may bring a suit. The court did not decide the claimant’s entitlement to succeed.

rule.if: civil_suit_for_succession and succession_case_outside_male_issue_rule and not civil_court_authorization_granted

predicates.civil_suit_for_succession: A claimant brought a civil suit seeking a determination of the right to succeed to an estate.
predicates.succession_case_outside_male_issue_rule: The succession question arose in circumstances not covered by the rule governing succession where there is male issue.
predicates.civil_court_authorization_granted: The government granted a certificate authorizing the succession matter to be determined by a civil court.

issues.definition: When a civil suit seeks a succession determination outside the male-issue succession rule and there is no authorization for civil court determination, the suit requires a prior administrative decision or civil court authorization.
